implementation_notes: uom makes the unit a type parameter: Quantity<D, U, V> holds dimension and unit phantom data plus a single value, so dimensional analysis is performed by the compiler at zero runtime cost - the crate's own pitch is that this is how you stop crashing your climate orbiter. Named quantities and units come from the generated SI system (uom::si::f64::{Length, Time}), Length::new::<kilometer>(3.0) constructs a value, .get::<meter>() reads a magnitude in a chosen unit, values are normalised to the quantity's base unit internally, and multiplication and division produce derived quantity types rather than raw numbers. A newtype per unit is justified only when the dependency is refused and the unit set is tiny.
pitfalls: Every boundary mentions the unit in a turbofish (Length::new::<kilometer>), which is noisy - define small constructor wrappers and convert once at the edge rather than everywhere.
Normalisation to the base unit means repeated conversion arithmetic; convert a value once outside a hot loop instead of calling .get::<u>() per iteration.
Carrying the phantom parameters through generic code is viral: a seam that takes f64 erases the guarantee exactly where data enters the system, so keep the typed form until serialization.

variants.name: Newtype per unit with explicit conversion
variants.implementation_notes: Without the dependency, a tuple-struct newtype per unit with a private field, a constructor per unit kind and explicit conversion methods gives the same unit safety for a small, fixed set: the type checker refuses to add Meters and Feet, and the conversions are the only way across. It is the pattern without dimensional algebra - compound units must be declared by hand - so it stays honest only while the unit set is small and no derived quantity is needed.
pitfalls: Deriving PartialEq compares the stored representation, so Meters(1000.0) and Feet(3280.84).to_meters() are only equal if the conversion is exact; normalise in the constructor or implement a tolerance-based comparison deliberately.
A public field or a From<f64> conversion makes the newtype decorative - it is the unit that must not be constructible without saying which unit it is.
Hand-written factors drift; keep one const table and generate or test both directions.
